questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle moving along a straight line in [Kinematics] has velocity $v = \alpha \sqrt{x}$, where $\alpha = 2\text{ m}^{1/2}\text{s}^{-1}$. At time $t = 0$, $x = 0$. Determine the acceleration of the particle and its velocity at $t = 3\text{ s}$.
questions.solution: Acceleration is $a = v \frac{dv}{dx} = (\alpha \sqrt{x})\left(\frac{\alpha}{2\sqrt{x}}\right) = \frac{\alpha^2}{2} = \frac{2^2}{2} = 2.0\text{ m/s}^2$. Since acceleration is constant, $v(t) = a t = 6.0\text{ m/s}$.
questions.explanation: Analyze the physical model and equations in Kinematics.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: One mole of ideal gas undergoes a polytropic expansion $P V^2 = C$ in [Kinematics] from volume $V_0 = 1\text{ m}^3$ at pressure $P_0 = 10^5\text{ Pa}$ to $V_1 = 2\text{ m}^3$. Calculate the magnitude of work done by the gas in $\text{kJ}$ rounded to nearest integer.
questions.solution: Work done in polytropic process with $n=2$: $W = \frac{P_0 V_0 - P_1 V_1}{n - 1} = P_0 V_0 \left(1 - \frac{V_0}{V_1}\right) = 10^5 \times 1 \times (1 - 0.5) = 5 \times 10^4\text{ J} = 50\text{ kJ}$.
questions.explanation: Calculate using quantitative physical laws in Kinematics.
